name: application-json-tree-viewer
title: JSON Tree Viewer
description: Collapsible key/value explorer with type-based coloring and expand-all/collapse-all controls, driven by a typed recursive data/expandedPaths prop contract.
useWhen: Displaying an API response, config object, or webhook payload for inspection or debugging.
Users need to drill into nested objects and arrays while collapsing branches they don't care about.
Data types (string, number, boolean, null) should be visually distinguishable at a glance.
avoidWhen: The hierarchy represents UI navigation or file/folder structure — use Tree View or File Tree instead, which carry different semantics.
The payload is small enough to read as flat formatted text — a plain code block is simpler.
Users need to edit values, not just inspect them — build a dedicated JSON editor instead.
responsiveBehavior: The panel scrolls horizontally within its own container so long keys or values never break the surrounding layout; height should be constrained by the parent for very large payloads.
accessibility: Expand/collapse toggles carry a dynamic aria-label naming the key so screen readers announce which branch will open or close.
Type coloring (string green, number orange, boolean blue, null italic gray) is a supplementary cue — the literal value text remains the source of truth.
Collapsed branches show an item count so users know content exists before expanding, aiding orientation without relying on color.

variants.title: JSON Tree Viewer
variants.description: Monospace key/value tree with per-branch expand/collapse, item-count summaries when collapsed, and header expand-all/collapse-all actions.
accessibility: Null values use italic styling in addition to color so they remain distinguishable without relying on color alone.

variants.title: JSON Tree Viewer (Dark)
variants.description: JSON explorer adapted for dark surfaces with the same expand/collapse, type-coloring, and count-summary structure.
accessibility: Type-coded value colors and key/punctuation text must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.
